keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kakuyid row): by 1008 Muhammad governed Isfahan (the 11th-century historian Mafarrukhi suggests he controlled it by 1003). The page says "c. 1008-c. 1051: Western Persia, Jibal, and Kurdistan" and gives no area; a 100 km circle at Isfahan stands for the early holding.

New keyframe: "1023 or 1024: Seized Hamadan." Hulwan, taken from the Annazids, was lost again after the Buyid Musharrif al-Dawla forced a withdrawal (the Kakuyids page gives no year for either; the Annazids page, reopened 2026-10-19, does not mention the Kakuyids at Hulwan), so it is not drawn; the war entry 'Kakuyid-Buyid war over Hamadan' records it.
New keyframe: the Annazid page: "1040: Alaa al-Dawla annexed Kermanshah and Dinavar" (read as the Kakuyid Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, 1008-1041); "1047: Muhalhil recaptured Kermanshah and Dinavar".

New keyframe: Hamadan lost in 1047 and Kermanshah and Dinavar lost to Muhalhil of the Annazids in 1047. Garshasp I page: "In 1047, the Seljuqs defeated his forces and seized Hamadan" (reign 1041-1047, then flight to Buyid Khuzestan); the Kakuyids page lists his rule as "(1041-1048)" without saying who took Hamadan, so 1047 follows the Garshasp I page. Isfahan alone holds to the Seljuk siege of 1051/1052. Neither page gives an area.

New keyframe: "After 1051/1052, the Seljuks granted Faramurz Yazd and Abarkuh in fief." The grant is two towns, not the province: reviewed 2026-10-19, drawn as a 65 km circle at Yazd and a 30 km circle at Abarkuh (about 16,000 km2; the earlier admin-1 Yazd drawing was 124,427 km2 and reached the Tabas district and the desert). The page gives no extent for the Yazd branch (Ali ibn Faramurz ruled Yazd in the 1070s-1095) and no infobox area; the fief is held to 1141 as the page's 'remained the governors of these provinces until sometime in the mid-12th century'.

ledger.note: 1008: Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, a Daylamite general of the Buyid amirate of Jibal, rules Isfahan. Infobox 'Established 1008'; 'By 1008 he governed Isfahan, a post his cousin Sayyida Shirin had secured for him.'

1023 or 1024: the Kakuyids seize Hamadan. 'Seized Hamadan. Then took Hulwan from the Annazids.' The page says "the Kakuyids invaded and took control of Hamadan in 1023 or 1024" in the Buyid succession after Shams al-Dawla (Sama' al-Dawla) and does not name the previous holder. Relation to the Buyids: the page has Muhammad "under the service of the Buyid amirate of Jibal" who "over time ... effectively became independent of Buyid control" and "at times ... acted as an ally of the Buyids", with no years. buyid-dynasty (me-08-c) carries a nominal-vassal tint for 1023-1029 (coins in Majd al-Dawla's name until 1029; its own page); the vassal tint is the suzerain's event, so no vassal pair is written here, and its counterpart string should be 'kakuyids' (it reads 'kakuyid-dynasty').

1040: Ala al-Dawla annexes Kermanshah and Dinavar. The Annazid page: '1040: Alaa al-Dawla annexed Kermanshah and Dinavar'; the identification with the Kakuyid Ala al-Dawla Muhammad (1008-1041) is the researcher's.
1047: the Annazids recapture Kermanshah and Dinavar. '1047: Muhalhil recaptured Kermanshah and Dinavar.'

1047: the Seljuks seize Hamadan from Garshasp I. 'In 1047, the Seljuqs defeated his forces and seized Hamadan' (Garshasp I page; he fled to Buyid Khuzestan). The Kakuyids page lists his rule over Hamadan, Nihawand, Borujerd and western Jibal as 1041-1048 and does not say who took it; the Garshasp I page is followed for the year and the taker. Counterpart great-seljuk-empire (me-09-a) should gain Hamadan in 1047.
1052: the Seljuks take Isfahan. 'After a year-long siege, the Seljuks took Isfahan in 1051 or 1052, ending Faramurz's rule there.'

1052: Faramurz receives Yazd and Abarkuh. 'After 1051/1052, the Seljuks granted Faramurz Yazd and Abarkuh in fief.' Drawn as the two towns (circles at Yazd and Abarkuh), not the province (reviewed 2026-10-19).
1141: the dynasty ends. Garshasp II was 'later killed at the Battle of Qatwan in 1141, the year the dynasty ended'; the Atabegs of Yazd succeed.

wars.name: Kakuyid-Buyid war over Hamadan
wars.outcome: The Kakuyids invaded Hamadan against Sama' al-Dawla (1023 or 1024) and took Hulwan from the Annazids; peace and a marriage alliance followed, and a Buyid withdrawal order cost them Hulwan but not Hamadan.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of Hamadan (1047)
wars.outcome: The Seljuks defeated Garshasp I and seized Hamadan in 1047; he fled to Buyid Khuzestan.

wars.name: Seljuk siege of Isfahan
wars.outcome: After a year-long siege the Seljuks took Isfahan in 1051 or 1052; Faramurz received Yazd and Abarkuh as a fief.
wars.note: The page gives the siege as "year-long" and the fall as 1051 or 1052; its start year is not given, so the span is recorded as 1051-1052.

certainty.note: City-based principality (Isfahan, Hamadan, then Yazd and Abarkuh); the page gives no frontiers or area.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Kakuyid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. The Ghaznavids, Tughril and Abu Kalijar are not on the page (nothing written from memory). Not written as events: the Hulwan gain from the Annazids (1023/24, lost again under Buyid pressure; the Kakuyids page gives no year and the Annazids page does not mention it; the 1023-1024 war entry records it); Garshasp I's hold on Nihawand and Borujerd (inside the Hamadan circle only in part); Ali ibn Faramurz at Yazd (1070s-1095); the Buyid alliance and marriage. Counterparts: annazids (not written), atabegs-of-yazd (successor; a new state a later group may write). The 1051 Isfahan siege start is not on the page. Ala al-Dawla is dated 1008-1041 (infobox); Garshasp II 1095-1141; the rulers between are in the text only. Gazetteer names needed: Abarkuh (drawn as a 30 km circle at 53.28E 31.13N).
Review fixes (2026-10-19, author): (1) The Seljuk fief 'Yazd and Abarkuh' was drawn as the whole Yazd province (124,427 km2, to 58.1E and 35.2N) for 89 years; now a 65 km circle at Yazd plus a 30 km circle at Abarkuh (about 16,000 km2) in the last keyframe, the 1052 gain, the 1141 dissolve and the atabegs-of-yazd successor land; the page gives no extent. Largest drawn keyframe is now 1040-1046 (Isfahan 100 km, Hamadan 80 km, Kermanshah province, Dinavar 50 km; about 77,000 km2 by the gazetteer), which has no page area to compare with (infobox: none, caption 'The Kakuyids at their greatest extent'). (2) Hamadan loss moved from 1048 (bridging, Seljuk reading) to 1047 on the Garshasp I page ("In 1047, the Seljuqs defeated his forces and seized Hamadan"; reign 1041-1047), against the Kakuyids page's '(1041-1048)'; the two keyframes 1047 and 1048-1051 became one (Isfahan only, 1047-1051). great-seljuk-empire (me-09-a) should therefore have a 1047 Hamadan gain with counterpart kakuyids. (3) Buyid relation: routed, not written as a vassal pair (the suzerain writes vassal_start/_end, with the Kakuyid as counterpart); the Kakuyids page gives no dates for service, independence or alliance; buyid-dynasty L14/L15 (Majd al-Dawla page, 1023-1029) should use the slug 'kakuyids'. The 1023 Hamadan event stays an outright gain from the Buyids, which is compatible with a nominal vassal tint afterwards. Disagreement with the reviewer: none; the Hulwan thin item could not be dated from either page and stays unwritten.
